Short answer: There is no settings.json key that points Claude Code at arbitrary extra skill roots (for example a custom path like ~/my-skills). Answer/Official from Manage Claude Code sessions and Agent view:
Is there any equivalent functionality in Claude/Code's CLI to Claude/Desktop/Code's ability to group related chat histories together?

Short answer: Nothing in the CLI matches Desktop's Code-tab sidebar (explicit repo/branch/worktree badges) directly, but the CLI has two mechanisms that get most of the way there: automatic directory-scoped grouping of session history, and an agent view (claude agents) that groups sessions by state or by directory.
Is there any equivalent functionality in Claude/Code's CLI to Claude/Desktop/Code's ability to group related chat histories together?

Directory-scoped grouping (implicit): the CLI stores each session transcript under ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl, keyed by working-directory path. Every session run from a given repo therefore already sits together on disk — an implicit grouping by project rather than an explicit tag or folder.
Is there any equivalent functionality in Claude/Code's CLI to Claude/Desktop/Code's ability to group related chat histories together?

Session picker: /resume (or claude --resume) opens a picker scoped to the current directory by default. From there: Ctrl+W expands to all worktrees, Ctrl+A expands to all projects on the machine, Ctrl+B filters by git branch, and text search matches names/summaries/PR URLs. Sessions can also be given a name (claude -n <name> or /rename) so related ones are easier to pick out.
Is there any equivalent functionality in Claude/Code's CLI to Claude/Desktop/Code's ability to group related chat histories together?

Agent view (closest analogue): claude agents opens a richer view that groups sessions either by state (Pinned, Ready for review, Needs input, Working, Completed — toggle with Ctrl+S) or by directory. Sessions can be pinned (Ctrl+T) to keep related ones at the top, filtered by agent name/state/PR number, and reordered within a group.
Is there any equivalent functionality in Claude/Code's CLI to Claude/Desktop/Code's ability to group related chat histories together?

What's still missing: no free-form tagging, no cross-repo logical grouping (grouping stays either state-based or directory-based, never topic-based), and no visual per-session metadata badges (repo/branch/worktree/env) like Desktop's Code tab shows in its sidebar.

What can the Microsoft 365 connector for Claude/Code do when viewing Excel sheets?

Short answer: There is no Excel-specific, cell-addressed tool. The Microsoft 365 connector treats an Excel workbook as an ordinary file in OneDrive/SharePoint: Claude Code finds it via search and opens and reads its content (sheet data, tables, text) via read_resource. It can analyze what it reads. It cannot edit individual cells or formulas in place — writes are whole-file operations, and only when the optional write tools are enabled. Everything is scoped to your own Microsoft 365 permissions.

What does the skill listing truncation warning in Claude/Code mean?
What does the skill listing truncation warning in Claude/Code mean?

What the message is: At the start of a turn, Claude Code injects a skill listing into the model context: each discoverable skill’s name plus (normally) its description and when_to_use text so the model knows what exists and when to load it. When that listing would use more than your configured share of the context window, the CLI drops full descriptions for the least-recently-used skills and keeps full text only for skills it considers most-used, then prints the warning you saw (with counts and an estimate of how much of the window the full listing would have taken versus the cap).
What does the skill listing truncation warning in Claude/Code mean?

Where it comes from: This behavior is implemented in Claude Code itself (not your shell). It is controlled by settings documented on Claude Code settings: skillListingBudgetFraction reserves a fraction of the model’s context window for that listing (default 0.01 = 1%). When the listing would exceed the budget, descriptions for the least-used skills are collapsed to bare names so the model can still invoke them but no longer sees why. A companion cap, maxSkillDescriptionChars (default 1536), truncates each skill’s combined description + when_to_use text before the overall budget is applied. See the same settings table rows and the skills guide Extend Claude with skills (frontmatter reference explains the listing and per-skill truncation).
What does the skill listing truncation warning in Claude/Code mean?

How to read the parenthetical (example 3.2% / 1%): The first figure is an estimate of how much of the context the full skill metadata would consume; the second is your current budget (often the default 1%). The gap is why many descriptions were dropped in one shot.
